raw_response:
I’m 48 this year, and with 20 years on these fields, I don’t like making big changes just because somebody says so. I finished middle school, so I can follow what the extension people say, but in the end I still trust what I’ve seen on my own land and what the better farmers nearby are doing. On 10.1 mu, I can’t afford to gamble. Wheat and maize together is the safest for me. Wheat needs enough base fertilizer and a topdress at jointing, otherwise it goes weak. Maize has to go in fast right after wheat harvest, so I won’t do fancy tillage, just quick residue handling and planting. We have a well, so if the rain misses at the key stage, I’ll irrigate, but I won’t pump water too many times because that costs money. I’ll use moderate fertilizer, not the highest rate, because some family members work off-farm and cash has to be kept a bit flexible.
